planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Robin forms an upright, vase-shaped habit and needs an open but sheltered site to flower well.

directions: Robin carries clusters of lightly scented, salmon-orange to red flowers with slender, wavy petals on bare branches from late winter into early spring, a deeper and warmer tone than many orange-flowered intermedia cultivars. Its broad, elliptic leaves turn a clear yellow in autumn before the winter bloom display begins. It develops an upright, eventually vase-shaped form and tolerates full sun as well as partial shade, provided the site is sheltered from strong wind. Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil that is neutral to slightly acidic, and prune only lightly right after flowering since next year's buds set soon afterward.
sources: Hillier Manual of Trees and Shrubs

common_name: Ripe Corn Witch Hazel (Dark Yellow Burgundy-Calyx Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Ripe Corn's dark-calyx flowers show best against an open, uncrowded backdrop.

directions: Ripe Corn opens slightly fragrant, dark yellow flowers with narrow, crimped petals set off by a dark burgundy-red calyx, a strong color contrast that stands out against bare branches in late winter and early spring. Broadly oval green leaves follow and turn attractive orange and yellow shades in autumn. It grows into an upright, often vase-shaped shrub and performs well in full sun or partial shade as long as it is sheltered from harsh wind. Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil that is neutral to slightly acidic, and limit pruning to light shaping immediately after bloom.

common_name: Alexander Witch Hazel (Orange-Red Pale-Spring-Leaf Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Alexander's pale spring foliage is a distinguishing feature worth siting where it can be seen up close.

directions: Alexander bears lightly scented, orange-red flowers with narrow, twisted petals on bare stems in late winter and early spring, typical of the intermedia group's winter display. What sets it apart is its spring foliage, which emerges a distinctive pale yellow-green before deepening to dark green over summer and then turning yellow and orange in autumn, giving the shrub a long season of color beyond the flowers alone. It forms an upright shrub and tolerates full sun as well as partial shade in a site sheltered from strong wind. Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, neutral to slightly acidic soil, and prune only lightly right after flowering.

common_name: Limelight Witch Hazel (Pale Yellow-Green Compact Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; young plants benefit from a sheltered position out of late frost pockets.

directions: Limelight stands apart from most intermedia witch hazels with very pale yellow flowers carrying a faint green cast, opening on bare branches from midwinter into early spring and giving a softer, more subdued winter display than the orange and red cultivars. Broadly oval green leaves turn yellow in autumn, and the shrub keeps a tidy, vase-like habit that stays noticeably smaller and more compact than many intermedia selections, making it easier to place in a modest-sized shaded border. Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil that is neutral to slightly acidic, in a site sheltered from wind and late spring frost, and prune only lightly right after flowering.

common_name: White Rim Pieris (Creamy White-Margined Pink-Flushed Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, sheltered from cold winds that can scorch the variegated foliage; White Rim is slow-growing and best given a permanent spot.

directions: White Rim is grown chiefly for its evergreen foliage, edged in bright creamy white and flushed pink as new leaves unfold before settling into a steady two-tone pattern year-round. Small white, urn-shaped flowers appear in dense, pendulous clusters in early to mid spring, though bloom can be lighter than on green-leaved Pieris cultivars. Its slow growth and dense habit suit a shaded foundation planting or container where the variegated foliage can be appreciated up close through the seasons. Site out of harsh winter wind and strong afternoon sun, which can scorch the pale leaf margins, and keep soil consistently moist, well-drained, and strongly acidic.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Passion is grown chiefly for its vivid spring foliage flush.

directions: Passion is valued above all for its new spring growth, which emerges a vivid red before gradually settling to deep green, giving the shrub a bright flush that lasts for several weeks each spring. Dense, upright to spreading clusters of urn-shaped flowers in shades of pink and white open at the same time, adding bloom color to the foliage display. It grows into a bushy, medium-sized shrub and performs best in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind. Prune lightly right after flowering only if needed, since next year's buds form soon afterward.

common_name: Cabernet Pieris (Compact Deep Red-Purple Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Cabernet is a compact selection bred for unusually deep flower color.

directions: Cabernet is distinguished by numerous deep red-purple, almost burgundy, flowers carried in clusters that hang horizontally to drooping from the branch tips, a markedly darker and richer tone than most Pieris cultivars. New leaves emerge a greyed red and mature to green, and the plant keeps a dense, freely branching, compact habit. It tends to flower a little later in the season than many other Pieris selections. Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and winter wind, and prune only lightly right after flowering if needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Select is a slow-growing, compact form well suited to smaller shaded beds.

directions: Select is a compact, slow-growing Pieris with slightly glossy, lance-shaped leaves that emerge coppery red before maturing to deep green, giving a long-lasting new-growth display. Fragrant white, urn-shaped flowers open from red-brown buds in hanging clusters each spring. Its restrained size and dense habit make it a practical choice for a smaller shaded border or foundation planting where larger Pieris cultivars would quickly need pruning to control. Grow in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from cold, drying winds, and mulch annually to help maintain soil moisture and acidity.

common_name: White Pearl Pieris (Compact Spreading White-Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; White Pearl is a free-flowering, compact selection suited to smaller shaded gardens and containers.

directions: White Pearl is a compact, slow-growing, spreading Pieris selected for its reliably heavy bloom, producing small, urn-shaped white flowers in upright clusters at the stem tips each spring in greater numbers than many other white-flowered cultivars. Its slightly glossy green foliage stays uniform year-round without the bronze or copper flush seen in many Pieris selections. The spreading, compact habit suits a city garden, patio container, or the front of a shaded border where a lower, wider shrub is wanted. Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh wind, and mulch annually in autumn.

common_name: Polar Passion Pieris (Cream-Edged Dwarf Deep Pink-Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Polar Passion is a dwarf, bushy selection well suited to small beds and containers.

directions: Polar Passion combines evergreen foliage edged in creamy white year-round with clusters of unusually deep reddish-pink, urn-shaped flowers produced at the stem tips each spring, a bolder flower color than most variegated Pieris selections. Its compact, bushy habit stays noticeably smaller than full-size Pieris japonica cultivars, making it a good fit for a small shaded bed, foundation planting, or large container. Grow in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from cold wind, and avoid chalky or waterlogged sites. Little pruning is needed beyond removing any shoots that revert to solid green.
